thread:
Alex: Quick sync — following the Saffron dedicated outage postmortem. Posting consolidated action items and owners here. Root causes: intermittent VPC peering flaps + on-prem routing constraints + an isolation bug in tenant namespace that allowed cross-tenant ARP replies.
OncallBot: Incident #SFF-2026-04-08 marked resolved. Severity: P1. Postmortem published.
Priya: Thanks — short summary from infra side: peering flaps were correlated with HTB queue drops on the edge router during burstups. On-prem team had a stale static route that dropped traffic to the dedicated pool.
Jamie: Noted recurring pattern: we've seen similar peering-related blips in the last 3 deploy cycles for Dedicated customers (Feb/Mar/Apr). I want a canary routing policy + synthetic peering check before any large rollout.
Luis: Filing the isolation bug now — RDW-3219. Brief: namespace isolation logic allowed ARP proxy responses when kernel neighbor table had stale entries; reproduced in lab with customer topology. Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RDW-3219
Maya: I'll own the VPC peering remediation. Plan: 1) add BFD monitoring on peer links; 2) tune edge queueing to avoid HTB overflow; 3) add preflight peering test to deploy pipeline. Target: initial fixes staged by 2026-04-14, full rollout by 2026-04-21.
Simon: For the on-prem static route issue — who will coordinate with the customer's network ops? We need a playbook.
Priya: I'll take customer coordination for the Saffron runbook. Action: send customer checklist + run it with their NOC. ETA: 2026-04-12.
Alex: Consolidated action items (please ack with :thumbsup: or assign alternative owner):
- RDW-3219 (Luis) — isolation bug, repro + patch PR, include regression test (deadline 2026-04-10)
- VPC peering hardening (Maya) — BFD + queue tuning + preflight test (stagelist 2026-04-14, rollout 2026-04-21)
- On-prem runbook + customer coord (Priya) — checklist + run NOC walkthrough (2026-04-12)
- Canary routing + synthetic peering monitor (Jamie) — add to deploy pipeline + dashboards (2026-04-16)
- Add historical incident pattern alerting (Simon) — correlate last 6 months peering flaps and flag repeat customers (2026-04-15)
Luis: Acknowledged. I'll attach the failing testcases to RDW-3219 and start the patch tomorrow.
Maya: Acked. I'll post patch notes and the staging playbook in #eng-infra once the BFD tests pass.
Jamie: I'll prototype the canary in the next 48h. Rough plan: run synthetic UDP/HTTP flows across peered path every 30s and alert on 5% packet loss over 2 min.
Simon: I'll wire up a query in the incidents dashboard to surface peering flaps per-customer and add a weekly digest.
Priya: One mitigation we can push immediately: enable conservative route aging on the customer-facing edge for Dedicated pools. I'll open a config change PR today (small blast radius).
Alex: Two follow-ups from product/security: 1) consider adding a fallback model routing for critical requests when dedicated pool shows isolation risk, 2) ensure audit log captures peering flaps with request IDs for cross-trace. Maya/Priya — can you handle items 1 & 2?
Maya: I can take the fallback routing policy design (will sketch by 2026-04-13).
Priya: I'll add the peering flap events to our audit pipeline and tag them with request IDs (ETA 2026-04-16).
Luis: One more note — the kernel repro required lowering arp_cache_validity to trigger the stale neighbor window. Test case included in RDW-3219.
Alex: Great. If no objections, we'll treat this as the canonical action list and track in the remediation tracker. I'll convert this thread into the action tracker rows after lunch. Please keep updates in this thread so timestamps line up.
Jamie: :thumbsup:
Maya: :thumbsup:
Luis: :thumbsup:
Priya: :thumbsup:
Simon: Will add dashboards and post progress in 2 days.
